6 of 15 layouts pages use demo.layout({twin:true}) — a 390-phone/3440-monitor comparison card. BOTH panes carry the same .demo-render class but are still zoomed to fit (escale 0.206 and 0.59 measured on mail/), so pointing at 'the render' does not fully escape the picture-of-a-layout problem for twins. These are exactly the three worst stage scores (mail 53, carousel 54, split 58), all driven by illegible on the zoomed pane, not a real layout defect.

one real, previously-invisible defect found: layouts/sidebar/ at 3440 measures ~178 characters per line in its article column (measure rule, high) — invisible to every audit run to date because probe.IGNORE has always skipped this box. Confirms the method's value independent of the twin caveat.

assign.outcome: **Measured 15 of the 132 mostly_picture page-widths at their stage's own render.** Median taste score is a wash (chrome 51 -> stage 53 at 1280) but that hides a real split: single-stage layouts pages (grid, sidebar, stack) score clean and sidebar's 3440 render surfaces a genuine, previously-invisible defect (~178 chars/line). The three numeric worst (mail 53, carousel 54, split 58) are a measurement artifact, not bad layouts: demo.layout({twin:true}) comparison cards keep BOTH panes zoomed (escale 0.206/0.59 measured), so illegible fires on a thumbnail, not the delivered page. Also caught empty false-firing on a deliberately sparse typography demo, and rate()'s covered:0 case defaulting to F. Recommend: a third 'stage' column on the existing audit/taste/ row (not a replacement, not a new page), gated on giving twin panes their own IGNORE exemption first -- verdict is Mike's.
